text: Shall the measure to amend Oakland's City Charter to, among other things, (1) make the Mayor the City's chief executive with a legislative veto, (2) empower the Council to override vetoes, confirm appointments of certain directors, and appoint an Independent Budget and Legislative Analyst, (3) affirm Councilmembers' right to acquire information from other City officials, (4) require Councilmembers to work full-time, and (5) empower the Public Ethics Commission to set salaries for all City elected officials using similar formulas, be adopted?
This measure would amend the Oakland City Charter to, among other things:

Make the Mayor the City’s chief executive. The Mayor, rather than the City Administrator, would manage most departments and appoint most department heads, except that the City Administrator would maintain authority over the departments of Human Resources and Finance. The Mayor would continue to appoint the City Administrator subject to Council confirmation.

Empower the Council to confirm the permanent appointments of the heads of the Human Resources and Finance departments, and the head of any department primarily responsible for designing, constructing, or maintaining City infrastructure. Currently, the Council does not confirm the appointment of any department head.
Empower the Council to create an Office of the Independent Budget and Legislative Analyst, which would provide independent fiscal, policy, and feasibility analysis to the Council.

Empower councilmembers to relay constituent concerns and propose projects to City staff; require City officials to respond promptly to councilmembers’ requests for information; and remove the provision that makes it a misdemeanor for councilmembers to interfere in administrative affairs.
Empower the Council to conduct legislative hearings and issue subpoenas to compel the production of documents or testimony.

Eliminate the Mayor’s existing power to cast tiebreaking votes when the Council is evenly divided, and empower the Mayor to veto legislation passed by the Council, with certain exceptions described in the measure. An affirmative vote of six councilmembers could override the Mayor’s veto, unless the legislation required more than six votes in order to pass, in which case an override would require the higher vote threshold.

Provide the Mayor a line-item veto over the annual budget, whereby the Mayor could veto any budget item adopted by Council and change it to the amount the Mayor originally proposed or to an amount somewhere between what the Council adopted and what the Mayor originally proposed. An affirmative vote of six councilmembers could override a line-item veto.
Require councilmembers to devote their full time to their office and prohibit councilmembers from engaging in outside employment or business that would interfere or conflict with their duties.

Require the Oakland Public Ethics Commission t o set t he sa la r ie s of t he Mayor a nd t he councilmembers, and require those salaries to be comparable to the salaries of similar full-time public officials in California. Currently the Oakland Public Ethics Commission adjusts the councilmembers’ salary by the consumer price index increase up to five percent, and the Council sets the Mayor’s salary in accordance with a formula based on comparably sized California cities.

Require publication of ordinances, either by newspaper or by another method authorized by the Council, within fifteen days of final passage. Currently this notice is published in a newspaper between introduction and final adoption.

Allow the Cou ncil to appoint a person to temporarily serve on the Council in place of the Council President if the Council President is filling a mayoral vacancy pursuant to the Charter. This measure was placed on the ballot by the City Council and will take effect only if a majority of voters voting on the measure vote “Yes.”
